OnPlay.rationale: RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-04 against current source (file re-shrunk since last audit; only line numbers moved, and the sim now fetches the returned power directly instead of re-fetching by id, which is a strictly stronger match to C#, not a divergence). `PowerCmd.Apply<InfernoPower>(..., DynamicVars["InfernoPower"].BaseValue, ...)` followed by `?.IncrementSelfDamage()` on the returned power (Inferno.cs:23) == `power = PowerCmd.apply(...)` then `if power is not None: power.increment_self_damage()` (inferno.py:38-42). Both reach the same instance and increment it exactly once per play on the normal path. Presentation, folded in: TriggerAnim (22).

guards.what: C# skips IncrementSelfDamage when Apply returns NULL; does the sim's read of the returned power correctly skip too? (Inferno.cs:23 vs inferno.py:38-42)
guards.rationale: REVISED 2026-08-04, faithful was gap -- the underlying source changed and closed this gap since the 2026-07-26 audit. The previous verdict described a STALE RE-FETCH: the sim used to call `PowerCmd.apply(...)` and then separately re-fetch the power `by id` (`ctx.player.get_power(InfernoPower.id)`) to call `increment_self_damage()`, which finds the OLDEST existing instance regardless of what the just-completed `apply()` call returned -- so a second Inferno whose amount was zeroed by a stacking modifier (Apply returns None, PowerCmd.cs guard) would still find and increment the pre-existing instance from the first Inferno. That re-fetch is GONE: current code (inferno.py:38-42) is `power = PowerCmd.apply(ctx.hooks, ctx.player, InfernoPower, self._power_amount, applier=ctx.player); if power is not None: power.increment_self_damage()` -- a direct use of `apply`'s own return value, which is `None` in exactly the same cases C#'s `Apply<T>` returns null (is_ending / CanReceivePowers refused / stacking amount resolves to 0; PowerCmd.apply docstring, cmds.py:860-882, and guard cmds.py:890-891). This now matches `PowerCmd.Apply<InfernoPower>(...)?.IncrementSelfDamage()` (Inferno.cs:23) exactly: skip on null, increment on the real returned instance otherwise. `card/crimson_mantle` (not part of this batch, but checked for rule-3 consistency) carries the identical shape at `crimson_mantle.py:37-41` -- same fix, same verdict; the card stream should confirm and update that record separately since it is outside this batch's 8-unit ownership. DORMANT-no-longer-applicable: the scenario this guard used to describe (Artifact zeroing a positive self-buff) cannot happen anyway (Artifact intercepts only debuffs, cmds.py:863), so even the OLD code's exposure was narrow; the direct-reference fix removes it regardless.
